Outline: Decompose the integrand into partial fractions, then integrate each fraction separately.
Step 1 — Partial fractions
Partial fractions: \( \frac{p(x)}{(x-a)(x-b)}=\frac{A}{x-a}+\frac{B}{x-b} \); a repeated factor \( (x-a)^2 \) gives \( \frac{A}{x-a}+\frac{B}{(x-a)^2} \); an irreducible \( x^2+bx+c \) gives \( \frac{Ax+B}{x^2+bx+c} \)
In order to calculate

\[ \int {{CT:0}} d{{CT:1}} \]

we need to express

\[ {{CT:0}} \]

as the sum of its partial fractions.

\[ \begin{aligned} {{CT:0}} &= {{CT:2}} \\ &= {{CT:3}}{{CT:4}} + {{CT:5}}{{CT:6}} + {{CT:7}}{{CT:8}} \end{aligned} \]

By multiplying both sides by {{CT:9}} we get

\[ \begin{aligned} {{CT:10}} &= {{CT:11}} + {{CT:12}} + {{CT:13}} \\ &= {{CT:14}} \end{aligned} \]

Equating coefficients of {{CT:15}} we get a system of equations that can be solved to get \(A = {{CT:16}}\), \(B = {{CT:17}}\) and \(C = {{CT:18}}\). So,

\[ {{CT:0}} = {{CT:19}} \]

Step 2 — Integrating term by term
Hence,

\[ \begin{aligned} \int {{CT:0}} d{{CT:1}} &= \int {{CT:19}} d{{CT:1}} \\ &= {{CT:16}} \int {{CT:4}} d{{CT:1}} {{CT:17}} \int {{CT:6}} d{{CT:1}} {{CT:18}} \int {{CT:8}} d{{CT:1}} \\ &= {{CT:20}} {{CT:21}} {{CT:22}} +c \\ &= {{CT:23}} +c \end{aligned} \]
